proceedings.deciding_body: Disciplinary Chamber of the QDC of Zakarpattya
proceedings.outcome: the applicant’s licence to practise as an advocate was suspended for six months
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 17 April 2013, in the applicant’s absence, the Disciplinary Chamber of the QDC of Zakarpattya suspended the applicant’s licence to practise as an advocate for six months for his failure to attend the meeting of 7 December 2012 and violating Article 62 of the Rules of Professional Conduct.

proceedings.outcome: the decision of 17 April 2013 was upheld
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 16 May the QDC of Zakarpattya upheld the decision of 17 April 2013.

proceedings.outcome: the draft decision to annul the previous decisions was rejected and the suspension remained valid
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 22 July 2016 the draft decision was put to vote at a HQDCB meeting where 19 out of 30 HQDCB members were present. Out of 19 members, 11 voted in favour of the decision, 6 voted against it, and 2 abstained. In view of the changes to the Rules of Procedure adopted in 2014 (see paragraph 16 above), the draft decision was rejected and the decisions suspending the applicant’s licence remained valid.

proceedings.outcome: examination of the appeal was suspended
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 16 February 2017 the Kyiv District Administrative Court granted the request and suspended the examination of the appeal of 5 October 2016.

proceedings.outcome: the court decided not to examine the applicant’s appeal
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 22 December 2016 the Podilskyy District Court decided not to examine the applicant’s appeal.

proceedings.outcome: the decision of 22 December 2016 was quashed
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 6 March 2017 the Kyiv Administrative Court of Appeal quashed the decision of 22 December 2016.

proceedings.outcome: found that all decisions issued by the self-government bodies of the Bar against the applicant had been lawful
proceedings.supporting_quote: On 8 April 2021 the Kyiv District Administrative Court found that all the decisions issued by the self-government bodies of the Bar against the applicant had been lawful.
The applicant’s appeals were rejected (final decision of the Supreme Court of 9 December 2021).
